posts.headline: "Rub it on and forget"
posts.subline: Maria G., New Zealand. Verified Judge.me review, Joints Rub
posts.caption:
Stiff joints are often worst first thing in the morning and after sitting still, and they can make summer feel smaller: shorter walks, less time in the garden.

What helps alongside a rub:
Move little and often. Short walks beat one long one.
Warmth for morning stiffness: a warm shower before you get going.
Keep the muscles around the joint strong with gentle exercise.

If a joint is suddenly hot, red and swollen, or the pain keeps you up at night, see your GP.

Two of our customers put it in their own words. Mavis from Huntly: "Excellent for my arthritis." Pam from Balclutha: "Excellent for my rheumatics."

Their words, not a promise: every body is different. Our Joints Rub is our higher-strength rub for stiffness and mobility, made with native herbs traditionally used for pain. Link in bio.

posts.title: Boxing Day recovery guide
posts.about: Education post for Boxing Day, from the dehydration blog article: why the day-after ache is often thirst, and the recovery order that helps, with a soft range mention last.
posts.headline: Is your Boxing Day ache actually thirst?
posts.subline: Water, movement, sleep. In that order.

steps.t: A big glass when you wake, then sip all day. Electrolytes if you sweated.
A gentle walk or swim gets blood moving through tight, tired muscles.
Massage a little rub into sore spots, then sleep. Sleep does the real work.

posts.caption:
Muscle aches the day after Christmas are often less about the cricket and more about the heat, the sun and the extra glass of bubbles. Even mild dehydration can leave muscles tight, crampy and sore.

Our Boxing Day recovery order:
1. Water first. A big glass when you wake, then keep sipping. Electrolytes if you sweated a lot.
2. Then move. A slow walk or a swim beats a day on the couch.
3. A rub before bed. Massage a little into the sore spots, then get a proper sleep.

If cramps are severe, or you feel dizzy or confused, see your GP or call Healthline on 0800 611 116.

For step three, our Sports range is the one we made for recovery, and Relief suits the whole family. Save this for the morning after.

posts.headline: The 2027 recovery routine we actually stick to
posts.subline: Three habits that do the real work

steps.t: Walk, swim or stretch on the days between harder sessions.
Seven to nine hours is when muscles do their repairing.
A few minutes after training or before bed, with a little rub.

posts.caption:
Recovery is not what you do once you are hurt. It is what you do every week so you are less likely to get hurt.

Our weekly routine for 2027:
1. Two easy days. Walk, swim or stretch between the harder days.
2. Sleep. Seven to nine hours is when muscles do their repairing.
3. Massage the sore spots. A few minutes after training or before bed.

If an ache turns into sharp pain or swelling, see your GP or physio before you push on.

Karlene from Auckland uses X-ZONE "before and after joint surgery, and when training."

For step three, our Sports Rub is the one we made for warm-up and recovery, and the Joints Rub suits stiffness that hangs around. Save this for the week ahead.

steps.t: Warm up, keep loads close, change position every 30 minutes.
Ease the grip load, strengthen gently, massage the forearm.

posts.caption:
Three injuries come up most on site: the lower back, the outer elbow and the shoulder. Each one builds slowly, so each one can be headed off.

Lower back: warm up, keep loads close, change position every 30 minutes.
Tennis elbow: ease the grip load, strengthen gently, massage the forearm.
Shoulders: break up overhead work, stretch at smoko, rub it in at the end of the day.

If pain comes with numbness, weakness or swelling, or it follows a fall, see your GP.

"Something that actually works really well." Ben M, electrician, Auckland.

For the end-of-day massage, our Sports Rub is made for hard-working muscles, and the Joints Rub for stiffness that hangs around. A jar in the ute makes it easy. Save this for smoko.

posts.headline: The first 48 hours decide your long weekend
posts.subline: What to do straight after a sprain

steps.t: Rest, ice wrapped in a cloth, compress and raise it for 48 hours.
Cold first, then gentle massage once the swelling settles.
Stop every two hours, walk, stretch, then rub it in.

posts.caption:
Long weekends bring long drives, new tracks and backyard games. Here's what to do in the first 48 hours if something hurts.

Rolled ankle: rest it, ice wrapped in a cloth for 15 to 20 minutes, a firm bandage, and keep it raised.
Bumps and bruises: cold first, then a gentle massage with a rub once the swelling settles.
Stiff after the drive: stop every two hours, walk and stretch.

If you can't put weight on it, the pain is severe, or something looks out of shape, see a doctor or call Healthline on 0800 611 116.

Our Relief range is the one for the bach or the car, for the bumps once the swelling settles.

However you spend the weekend, we hope it is a good one with whānau. Save this for the drive.

sections.b: A bruise changes colour as it heals. Red to purple: day one or two, so a cold pack in short bursts helps. Blue to green: days three to six, when gentle warmth and light massage around the spot can help. Yellow to brown: about a week in, nearly there. See your GP if a bruise appears for no reason, is very large, sits over a joint you can't move, or isn't fading after two weeks.

Start with the person, not the product. The tradie with a sore back and shoulders: the Sports Rub. The tramper with tight calves on day two: a roll-on for the pack. hero.headline: Stiff joints this summer? Here is what helps
hero.subline: Three habits, the 10% rule, then the Joints Rub

sections.b: Joint stiffness is often worst first thing in the morning and after sitting still: the long drive to the bach, an afternoon in the deck chair. Gentle movement keeps joints comfortable and the muscles around them strong, so the best answer to stiffness is usually little and often, not rest.

Move little and often: short walks beat one long one. Warmth for morning stiffness: a warm shower before you get going. Keep the muscles around the joint strong with gentle exercise. And if the new year means more walking, gardening or training, add no more than about 10% a week. If a joint is suddenly hot, red and swollen, or the pain keeps you up at night, see your GP.

Our Joints Rub is our higher-strength rub for stiffness and mobility, made with native NZ herbs traditionally used for pain, with 11 to 14 active ingredients where most rubs use five or six. In independent lab tests (Trinity Bioactives, 2024), the Joints Rub reduced inflammation-associated cells by 48.1%. These were in-vitro tests on cells, not a clinical trial on people. Massage it in for a minute, best after a warm shower. Trial pots start from $3 if you would like to try it first.

emails.preheader: DOMS explained, plus what independent lab tests found when they tested our three rubs.
emails.title: DOMS and the lab results
emails.about: Week 7 newsletter: the DOMS lesson from Monday's carousel, the Trinity Bioactives in-vitro results from Friday's post, and the unscheduled hamstring tip from w7-sat.

hero.headline: Why day two hurts more than day one
hero.subline: DOMS in plain English, and what the lab found

sections.b: The soreness that turns up two days after a big session is DOMS, delayed onset muscle soreness. New or harder work leaves tiny strains in muscle fibres, and repairing them takes time. It is not lactic acid. What helps: keep moving gently, drink water, eat some protein, sleep well and massage the sore muscles. A sudden, sharp pain at the back of the thigh is different: stop and see a physio or GP.

In independent in-vitro lab tests by Trinity Bioactives in 2024, our Sports Rub reduced inflammation-associated cells by 54.1%, the Joints Rub by 48.1% and the Relief Rub by 42.7%. These were tests on cells in a lab, not a clinical trial on people. We share them because you deserve to see the science behind what goes on your skin.

hero.headline: Heat or ice? The honest answer
hero.subline: It depends on how new the pain is

sections.b: Ice is for new injuries: a fresh sprain, a knock or anything swelling in the first 48 hours. Wrap it in a cloth, 15 to 20 minutes, never straight on the skin. Heat is for stiffness: a tight lower back, a sore neck, muscles that ache after a long day. Morning joint stiffness often prefers warmth. A joint that is suddenly hot, red and swollen is worth a GP visit.

Ceilings, gutters, painting and pruning leave the muscles around the shoulder tight and tired. At the end of the day, massage a rub into the top and back of the shoulder for a minute, then finish with slow arm circles. If your shoulder catches with pain, will not lift above your head, or the ache wakes you at night, see your GP or physio.

emails.title: Tennis elbow and site backs
emails.about: Week 9 tradie-week newsletter: tennis elbow from the unscheduled w9-wed post, the lower-back habits from Monday's carousel, and Friday's three site injuries.

hero.headline: Tennis elbow isn't just tennis
hero.subline: Gripping, drilling, pruning and scrolling all count

sections.b: Tennis elbow is pain on the outside of the elbow, and most people who get it have never held a racquet. It comes from the same small movement repeated: gripping a drill, painting a ceiling, pruning. What helps: ease the load by changing grip or swapping hands, build strength back gently once the sharp pain settles, and massage the forearm morning and night. If it came from a fall, or your hand is numb or weak, see your GP.

sections.h: Five free habits for your back
sections.b: Warm up for two minutes before the first lift. Keep the load close and turn with your feet. Change position every 30 minutes. Ask for a hand with the heavy stuff. Look after the drive home and your sleep. Back pain with numbness, weakness, pain down a leg, or any change to your bladder or bowel needs your GP straight away.

emails.subject: Sleep is recovery
emails.preheader: Three free sleep habits, and which common medicines can be linked to muscle aches.
emails.title: Sleep and medicine aches
emails.about: Week 10 newsletter: sleep habits from Friday's post, the medicines-and-muscle-pain lesson from Monday's carousel, and the unscheduled hands-and-wrists tip from w10-sat.

hero.headline: The best recovery tool is free, and it's your bed
hero.subline: Three sleep habits, and when a medicine is behind the aches

sections.b: Your body does most of its repair while you sleep, and no product beats a good night. Keep the same wake time every day, weekends too. Make the room cool, dark and quiet, with the phone out of reach. Give yourself thirty minutes of wind-down off screens. A slow massage into whatever aches is a good way to tell your body the day is over.

sections.h: When a medicine and aches arrive together
sections.b: Some common medicines are linked to muscle aches as a side effect, including statins for cholesterol, some antibiotics and longer courses of steroid tablets. It doesn't happen to everyone. The important thing: don't stop a prescribed medicine on your own. Write down when the aches started and talk to your GP or pharmacist. Check with your pharmacist that a rub suits you alongside your medicines.

hero.headline: The five minutes that save your long weekend
hero.subline: First aid, a quick warm-up and the Sports Rub

sections.b: Long weekends bring long drives, new tracks and backyard games. Rolled ankle: rest it, ice wrapped in a cloth for 15 to 20 minutes, a firm bandage, and keep it raised. Bumps and bruises: cold first, then a gentle massage once the swelling settles. Stiff after the drive: stop every two hours to walk and stretch. If you can't put weight on it, see a doctor or call Healthline on 0800 611 116.

Most weekend sports niggles start in the first ten minutes, on cold muscles. A brisk walk or easy jog, ten arm circles each way, leg swings front to back, then a few gentle build-ups to speed. Afterwards, walk it off and stretch while you are still warm. Sharp pain that stops you mid-game is a signal to stop, not to push on.

Our Sports Rub is the higher-strength rub we made for warm-up and recovery, with native NZ herbs traditionally used for pain. In independent lab tests (Trinity Bioactives, 2024), the Sports Rub reduced inflammation-associated cells by 54.1%, the highest of our three rubs. These were in-vitro tests on cells, not a clinical trial on people. Massage it in before you start and again afterwards. Trial pots start from $3.

This summer we shared the eleven native herbs behind X-ZONE, each one traditionally used in rongoā rākau, Māori plant medicine. That knowledge belongs to Māori, and our job is to credit it properly. The full eleven-herb guide is on our blog. However you spend Waitangi weekend, we hope it is a good one with whānau.

Ngā mihi, Jess and Dan

emails.title: The sideline kit for parents

hero.headline: What smart sideline parents keep in the car
hero.subline: What to pack, and when to sit them out

sections.b: School's back, so Saturday sport is back, and so are the knocks. Pack it once and leave it in the car: water, snacks, an ice pack, a bandage, plasters and sunscreen. Knocks and bruises: cold for 15 minutes, then a gentle massage once the swelling settles. Rolled ankles: off the field, rest, ice, a firm bandage, and no more play until it is pain-free.

If your child has a knock to the head and seems dazed, sick, sleepy or not themselves, take them off and see a doctor. When in doubt, sit them out. And before trials, a 20-second warm-up helps: high knees, side shuffles, calf raises, then small hops landing soft with knees over toes.

hero.headline: Thank you for a summer of learning with us
hero.subline: Now help us choose what we cover this autumn

sections.b: Thirteen weeks ago we set out to teach, not just sell. You saved the first-aid posts, learned eleven native herbs with us and sent us your questions. Every one of those shapes what we make next. Ngā mihi nui.

Which one is right for me? Relief for everyday aches and the family, Joints for stiffness and mobility, Sports for warm-up and recovery. How much should I use? 1 to 5 ml, massaged in, up to five times a day, best after a shower. Patch test first. Heat or ice? Ice for a fresh injury in the first 48 hours, gentle warmth for stiff muscles and joints.

Choose this autumn's topics: arthritis and stiff joints through winter, getting back into sport after 50, more herb stories from the bush, or something else entirely. It takes two minutes, and Jess and Dan read every answer. This week on Instagram and Facebook: your twelve most-saved posts, our top Reel of the summer, and the questions you asked most.

Cooler mornings are coming, and stiff joints notice them first. Our Relief, Joints and Sports ranges are online and in 200+ stores around Aotearoa when you need them.

Ngā mihi, Jess and Dan
